Updated the data map alongside the retention change, so practice and paper agree; the privacy review has the diff and confirmed the audit line item closes with it.

The tenant notification templates for quarantined batches also read like a stack trace wearing a tie. Rewrite them so an integrator learns what was held, why, and what to fix, without needing one of us on a call to translate the rejection code. Run the rewritten templates past the developer-experience folks before they ship, because the last wording change confused two integrators into re-sending held batches in a loop and the queue graphs looked like an attack.

Rewrote the templates around the rejection taxonomy with a fix-it link per code family; the integrator support channel already noticed the difference in the trial tenant. The developer-experience folks reviewed the wording and the templates now explicitly say not to re-send held batches; the trial tenant's behaviour confirms the loop pattern is gone.

Quarantine visibility is still thin on the admission board: depth is there but age is not, and an old held batch is the actual signal that something is wedged rather than merely bursty. Add oldest-held-age panels split by tenant next to the depth ones. Backfill the age panels from the retained history where possible too, because a panel that starts empty tonight cannot distinguish a wedge that began last week from one that began at panel creation.

Added oldest-held-age panels beside the depth panels with the per-tenant split; the board now distinguishes a wedge from a burst at a glance. Backfilled age history from the retained hold records, so the panels open with a week of context and a pre-existing wedge reads as old on day one instead of hiding as new.

And drop the admission log back from the incident verbosity; it has been logging every accepted batch for three weeks and the log budget graph is a ski jump. Keep the verbose form for rejections only. Make the verbosity change through the logging config layer rather than the code path, so the next incident can turn accepted-batch logging back on with a reload instead of waiting on a deploy.

Dropped accepted-batch logging back to the normal level, kept verbose rejection logging, and the log budget graph is already flattening. Moved the verbosity control into the logging config layer with a reload hook; incident responders can flip it live, and the setting documents its own log-budget cost next to the flag.

Scope note so the thread stops resurfacing: the 2000-batch quarantine cap from the incident draft is dead; it was sized for the old single-lane spool and quoting it in sizing threads just muddies the review.
Marked the draft dead with a superseded banner and linked the current sizing sheet; the number should stop leaking into threads now.
